title: PCT: Point Cloud Transformer
grouping: No containers: the module runs as one left-to-right chain with a skip line along the bottom from the input to the subtraction and to the final adder, and a top line carrying the input to the value branch. A two-row legend under the drawing names every tensor colour and operator glyph.
shapes_depth: Tensors are 3-D slanted slabs with rounded edges and a light-to-dark gradient, each role in its own saturated colour (input light blue, query orange, key teal, attention map large blue, value magenta, attention feature purple, output dark navy; Linear and LBR as pale-green slabs). Slab proportions follow the tensor shape: the d_a x N key lies flat, the N x N attention map is the largest. Italic shape labels (N x d, N x d_a, N x N) sit above the slabs. Operators are light-blue circles with times / plus / minus glyphs and small square boxes (T, SS, SL); a lever-like switch glyph selects between the dotted SS path and the solid SL path. Thick black orthogonal arrows.
proposed_highlight: The module's change is carried by the subtraction circle that takes input minus attention feature and by the switch choosing SL over SS; nothing is boxed or coloured as 'new' - the legend does the naming.
lesson: Give each tensor role its own colour and a 3-D slab whose proportions follow its shape (flat key, large square attention map), and decode colours and operator glyphs in a legend row underneath so the drawing itself carries only shape labels.
notes: Venue Computational Visual Media from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2012.09688). elements 'other' = the switch glyph. A user-layer card of Figure 2 (PCT architecture) exists; this is Figure 3. The gradient-shaded 3-D slabs are embedded rasters (drawn parts, not photos), so measured photo_share counts them and the palette leaves them out.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: point cloud classification and segmentation (offset-attention module)

core.what: one left-to-right chain of colour-coded tensor slabs and operator circles computing offset attention, with the input carried along the bottom to a subtraction (input minus attention feature) and a final addition

relations.form: left to right: input slab, linear, query and key slabs, matrix-multiply circle, SS/SL normalisation boxes, N x N attention map, multiply with value, attention feature, subtract, LBR, add, output slab
query and transposed key lines converge on one multiply circle; the attention map and the value (brought by a line over the top from the input) converge on a second multiply circle

a lever-shaped switch selects between the SS (scale + softmax, dotted path) and SL (softmax + l1 norm, solid path) branches, and a second switch selects the offset (subtract) path over the dotted plain-attention exit
the input is reused by a long line along the bottom of the figure that feeds both the subtract circle and the final add circle

channels.colour: one saturated colour per tensor role: light blue input, orange query, teal key, blue attention map, magenta value, purple attention feature, navy output; pale green linear and darker green LBR layers, as keyed in the legend
channels.shape: slanted 3-D slabs = tensors, proportioned to their shape (flat key, large N x N map); circles = matrix multiply/add/subtract; small rounded boxes = normalisation and transpose ops; lever glyph = switch
channels.line: solid = the path taken in offset attention, dotted = the alternative (SS / plain attention) path not taken
channels.frame: none; a two-row legend strip underneath keys every glyph

quality.strengths: Every intermediate representation (query, key, attention map, value, attention feature) is drawn as its own slab whose shape follows its tensor size, between the operation that makes it and the one that consumes it; the offset is visible as a subtract circle fed by the input along the bottom; the switches make the two design choices explicit.
quality.weaknesses: Seven tensor colours plus two layer greens require a legend lookup for each slab; the input's two reuse lines (over the top to value, along the bottom to subtract/add) run the full width of the figure; operator circles carry only symbols so the meaning of each is legend-dependent.

insights.structure: No containers: one left-to-right chain of tensors and operators with a skip line running along the bottom from the input to the subtraction and the final adder, and a top line carrying the input to the value branch; a two-row legend underneath.
insights.data: Tensors are 3-D slanted slabs with gradient shading, one saturated colour per role (input light blue, query orange, key teal, attention map blue, value magenta, attention feature purple, output navy), with proportions following shape (flat key, largest N x N map) and italic shape labels above.
insights.emphasis: The offset-attention change is carried by the minus circle (input minus attention feature) and a lever-like switch selecting the solid SL path over the dotted SS path; the legend names everything.
insights.flow: Thick black orthogonal arrows run left to right, with the key branch dipping below via a T (transpose) box and the long input skip running along the bottom edge.
insights.avoid: The dotted alternative paths (SS, the dotted arrow after the attention feature) end in open space, and the switch glyph is not self-explanatory without the legend.

arrangement.units: one unframed chain of tensor slabs and operator circles/boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: a light-blue 3-D slab labelled N x d
